今天 cash-cat:native 最低到了150M，在Hyperliquid上的合约更是插针到了80M，带着Robinhood链上的Meme集体回调了一波。

这一波RH的行情，我印象里参考性比较强的，是之前类似的两次公链上的Meme热潮。

一次是24年8月末的Tron，由$Sundog带头，高点接近400M，也催生了一批峰值30~50M的Meme币，后续$Sundog上了HTX、Bybit等交易所，但最终没有进一步登陆一线大所，一个月后开始慢慢阴跌，其余的Meme币生命周期则更短。

另一次是24年末到25年初的Base行情，当时先经历了一波由$Brett领头的百花齐放，高点2.3B，并带动了一批突破100M的Meme币，例如$Keycat、$Miggles等，然后经过一个月的回调，在1月中旬由$Toshi进入Coinbase Roadmap的消息再度引燃，高点达到了960M，许多生态代币也在带动下由底部反弹了3~5倍，整个行情前后持续了接近三个月。

对比来看的话，我认为RH这波链上行情，更有机会走出Base的轨迹，首先两者分别有Robinhood和Coinbase两个一线交易所作为背书和潜在上币通道，从近期Sol官方与Robinhood的频繁互动也能看出这一点的重要性。其次当时的Base除了Meme币，还有$Degen和Farcaster生态下的各种应用币，而现在的RH则有$Arrow、$VEX等RWA和AI Agent题材的应用币，更广泛的题材也意味着更持久的生命力。

目前最关键的，还是 cash-cat:native 的走势，如果可以在每次回调后都走出反弹，并维持住上Robinhood的预期，直至最终顺利上币，那么整个生态都将持续存在机会。而经过今天的回调后，目前市值龙二的Meme币应该是 hoodrat-4:native ，作为Matt Furie的笔下角色，Pepe系几乎是每条新链的Meme行情都会出现的一个金狗题材，我会密切关注这两个代币的走势作为RH链上建仓和抄底的选择。

1. The tech is already developed and fees are super low. I'm not sure spam will be reduced at all by existing users, but even if it reduces *moderately* then none of this is existential as it's often marketed. Spam could also reduce over time naturally as NFTs/memecoins deteriorate in value and/or if average monetary transaction fees rise from demand (a good scenario, more people transacting in bitcoin).\n\n4. For op return, people have routed to miners through networks of nodes with wider settings than the default, rather than each one having to go directly to miners. You surely know this since I'm not as technical and I know this. Capping op return, as I've said and as you readily admit, still maintains many other methods of spam. For the witness updates, I've never made the claim that every technical detail (or even most technical details) of this fork is bad. In the interview I even said if these rules had been in from earlier, I'd be fine with them. There are several forks out there that I support parts of, which simply haven't garnered enough support for consensus yet. The issue I've raised is marketing the fork as being existential, that bitcoin dies if this doesn't pass, that people who oppose it or ignore it are bad, when ultimately what it does is narrow some methods of spam while preserving many others including the cheapest methods (since it's impossible to cut out all of them).

1. VC money for that has already mostly gone elsewhere. It was a fad like other shitcoin projects. Nobody has to “find” a new hack for witness spam; they’re already published now.\n\n4. That method has been possible in consensus for over a decade. It’s just that people use it now (starting in the months pre-Core30, as you know). Yet it’s being marketed as existential risk now, literally saying Bitcoin will fail otherwise, despite it not being the cheapest way to spam.
